fine_lines.title: my vs mine
fine_lines.explanation_ar: my صفة ملكية يأتي بعدها اسم: my bag. mine ضمير ملكية يقف وحده بدون اسم: The bag is mine. وكذلك your/yours، her/hers، our/ours، their/theirs. أما his فهي نفسها في الحالتين.
fine_lines.explanation_en: "My" comes before a noun: my bag. "Mine" stands alone: The bag is mine. The same with your/yours, her/hers, our/ours, their/theirs. "His" is the same in both cases.

fine_lines.title: its vs it's
fine_lines.explanation_ar: its بدون فاصلة علوية = ملكية لغير العاقل (له/لها). it's = it is. وضمائر الملكية لا تأخذ فاصلة علوية أبداً: yours, hers, ours, theirs.
fine_lines.explanation_en: "Its" (no apostrophe) shows possession for a thing or animal. "It's" means "it is". Possessive pronouns never use an apostrophe: yours, hers, ours, theirs.

examples.sentence: The city is famous for its museums.

fine_lines.title: agree vs disagree
fine_lines.explanation_ar: agree = لديك نفس الرأي. disagree = لديك رأي مختلف. البادئة dis تعطي العكس. نقول agree with someone ولا نقول I am agree.
fine_lines.explanation_en: "Agree" means you have the same opinion; "disagree" means a different one. The prefix dis- makes the opposite. Say "I agree", not "I am agree".

examples.sentence: I disagree. I like the city.

grammar.title: Possessive pronouns: mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs
grammar.explanation_ar: ضمائر الملكية تحل محل (صفة الملكية + الاسم) حتى لا نكرر الاسم: Is this your bag? → Is this bag yours? الجدول: I → my → mine، you → your → yours، he → his → his، she → her → hers، we → our → ours، they → their → theirs. لا تأتي بعدها أسماء ولا نضع معها فاصلة علوية.
grammar.explanation_en: Possessive pronouns replace "possessive adjective + noun" so we don't repeat the noun: Is this your bag? → Is this bag yours? I → my → mine, you → your → yours, he → his → his, she → her → hers, we → our → ours, they → their → theirs. No noun comes after them and no apostrophe.
examples: No. It's not mine. It might be hers.
They have their opinions. We have ours.

grammar.title: Comparing with more ... than
grammar.explanation_ar: للمقارنة بين الكميات نستخدم more + اسم + than: The city has more culture than the country. ونستخدم more بدون than عندما يكون الطرف الثاني واضحاً: There are more jobs.
grammar.explanation_en: To compare amounts use more + noun + than: The city has more culture than the country. Leave out "than" when it is clear: There are more jobs.
examples: The city has more culture than the country.
There are more trees and mountains.

grammar.title: Agreeing and disagreeing politely
grammar.explanation_ar: للموافقة: I agree. / That's a good point. للاعتراض: I disagree. / I don't think... ويمكن أن نوافق على جزء ونعترض على آخر: Well, I agree... But I don't think...
grammar.explanation_en: To agree: I agree. / That's a good point. To disagree: I disagree. / I don't think... You can agree with one part and disagree with another: Well, I agree... But I don't think...
examples: Well, I agree. Country people are friendly.
But I don't think city people are rude.
I disagree. I think the buildings are beautiful.
